sources.title: Model Release Notes — o3-pro, June 10, 2025
sources.evidence: The dated entry launches o3-pro in ChatGPT and the API on June 10, 2025, with Pro and Team access that day and Enterprise/Edu the following week. It explicitly says o3-pro uses the same underlying model as o3 and directs readers to the o3 system card. It identifies longer reasoning, visual inputs and tools. ChatGPT image generation and canvas were unsupported at launch.

sources.title: o3-pro model reference
sources.evidence: Read the complete current Markdown reference and the documentation connector response. The exact model has snapshot o3-pro-2025-06-10, 200,000 context tokens, 100,000 maximum output tokens, text/image input, text output, reasoning, function calling, structured outputs, Responses and Batch. It is deprecated. Hosted Responses tools include file search, web search, MCP and image generation; image generation is not a native output modality. The exact pro model has no cached-input price or prompt_caching feature in this reference.

sources.title: API changelog — June 10, 2025
sources.evidence: The June 10 entry explicitly releases o3-pro, a version of o3 using more compute, for Responses and Batch. This independently corroborates the first-public-release date; the date is not inferred only from the API snapshot identifier.

sources.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded and searched the full original PDF, and inspected model data/training and evaluation sections. The card describes large-scale reinforcement learning on chains of thought and tool use but does not give o3 production total/active parameter counts or dense/MoE topology. It predates o3-pro; its relevance is established by the June 10 release note explicitly linking the shared underlying model, not by assuming all o-series variants share internals.

sources.title: o3 model reference
sources.evidence: The exact o3 reference documents prompt_caching and cached-input prices for o3-2025-04-16. Together with the o3-pro same-underlying-model statement and the applicable archived caching engineering explanation, this supports a qualified broad Transformer inference. It does not establish that the o3-pro API itself supports prompt caching.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Read the archived recipe. It expressly applies to models before GPT-5.6, explains OpenAI request processing through Transformer layers and attention Q/K/V projections, and explicitly discusses o3 caching. This supports broad Transformer structure for the bound underlying o3 model, not production layer counts, size, expert routing or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded the complete later PDF and inspected its model progression and comparison tables. Table 1 names OpenAI o3 Pro as predecessor to gpt-5-thinking-pro. Tables 2, 3 and 5, among others, have exact OpenAI o3 evaluation columns, but report behavioral scores, not parameter counts. The full-text count/topology search found no o3-pro or o3 production count disclosure. The parallel-test-time-compute description is for GPT-5 pro and is not transferred to o3-pro.

sources.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded the complete later OpenAI report and inspected the architecture/count table and closed-model comparison discussion. Table 1 discloses total/active counts only for the two gpt-oss models. Later sections and Figure 4 compare exact OpenAI o3 performance, not o3-pro parameter counts. Those open-model counts and MoE details cannot be transferred to o3 or o3-pro.

sources.title: Detecting and reducing scheming in AI models
sources.evidence: Read the first-party research article, including its model/training discussion. It describes experimental versions of o3 and o4-mini trained using deliberative alignment and internal reasoning access; it supplies no production o3-pro parameter counts or architecture dimensions. The article does not bind those experimental weights to the released pro snapshot.

sources.title: Toward understanding and preventing misalignment generalization
sources.evidence: Read the first-party interpretability article while searching for o3 structural disclosures. Its sparse-autoencoder feature analysis concerns GPT-4o and its reasoning fine-tuning experiments concern o3-mini, not the released o3-pro. Neither feature counts nor those other models supply o3-pro parameter counts or topology.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: The current guide states that Responses accepts PDF input files and, for vision-capable models, sends extracted text and page images to the model. The exact o3-pro card establishes its vision and Responses support. PDF is therefore recorded as an API input format, not a separate native neural modality. The older pdf-files page redirects here; the old .md path returned 404, after which the canonical .md was successfully retrieved.

sources.title: API deprecations — GPT-5 and o3 model deprecations
sources.evidence: The June 11, 2026 notice explicitly lists o3-pro and o3-pro-2025-06-10 for removal on December 11, 2026. At the October 27 audit date this is a scheduled future shutdown, not an already completed shutdown. No live API call was made.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5
sources.evidence: The August 7, 2025 launch describes GPT-5 pro replacing OpenAI o3-pro in ChatGPT. That product replacement is distinct from the o3-pro API deprecation schedule. Its GPT-5 architecture and compute details are not transferred to o3-pro.

name.note: Exact developer model name, distinguished from ordinary o3 and o3-deep-research.

developer.note: OpenAI publishes and serves the exact model.

family.note: Use o3 generation grouping within the broader o-series. The release also explicitly binds this pro version to the underlying o3 model; this grouping does not assert that every o3-named variant shares weights.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is June 10, 2025 in ChatGPT and the API; the next-week Enterprise/Edu rollout is not the original release. The exact API snapshot has the same date.

open_weights.note: Released as an OpenAI-hosted ChatGPT/API model, with no downloadable production checkpoint or open-weight license in the inspected release materials.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted closed-weight model; no open-weight license is offered. This is not an SPDX identifier or a license for user outputs.

parameters_b.note: No total production parameter count was disclosed in the checked exact-model materials, the explicitly bound original o3 card, later GPT-5 and gpt-oss comparison material, or searched training/interpretability research. Higher inference compute does not imply more model parameters.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count or dense/MoE routing specification was disclosed for the exact model. Do not equate active and total counts or import the gpt-oss active-count convention.

architecture.note: Qualified broad inference: the June 10 release says o3-pro uses the same underlying model as o3; exact o3 caching support binds it to OpenAI’s applicable pre-GPT-5.6 explanation of Transformer layers and Q/K/V attention. This does not establish prompt caching in the pro API, dense versus MoE, layer counts or parameter counts. The original card provides training information, not an exact topology.

context_window.note: Exact o3-pro-2025-06-10 reference gives 200,000 context tokens and a separate 100,000 maximum output limit. These are documented limits; endpoint operation was not tested.

modalities.note: Native input is text and image, with text output. PDF is additionally supported as a Responses file format parsed into text/page images. Hosted image generation is a separate tool, not native model output; launch-era ChatGPT restrictions are not generalized to later API tool support.

reasoning.note: The exact model uses more computation to reason before responding and supports reasoning tokens. No unsupported claim about parallel sampling or a specific test-time algorithm is made.

tool_call.note: Exact API documentation supports function calling, plus hosted Responses tools including file search, web search and MCP. ChatGPT launch tools also include file analysis and Python; product tool availability is not treated as native modality.

description.value: OpenAI o3 reasoning variant that uses more inference compute, with text and image input and function calling.
description.note: Neutral factual replacement for the promotional baseline description, without unqualified performance or reliability claims.

patch.notes: The o3-pro alias points to o3-pro-2025-06-10. OpenAI explicitly identifies the underlying model as o3, with additional inference compute; this does not disclose total or active parameter counts. Transformer is a broad inference from that binding, exact o3 prompt-caching support and OpenAI’s applicable pre-GPT-5.6 engineering explanation. It does not imply prompt caching in the o3-pro API or disclose dense/MoE topology. The API supports Responses and Batch, with 200,000 context tokens and 100,000 maximum output tokens. PDF is an API input format converted into text and page images; hosted image generation is not native image output. GPT-5 pro replaced o3-pro in ChatGPT in August 2025. The o3-pro API is deprecated with removal scheduled for December 11, 2026; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirmed the June 10, 2025 public release and exact API specifications. Corrected family to o3, added descriptive Proprietary licensing, a qualified broad Transformer inference through the explicit same-underlying-model binding, and PDF input-format support; replaced promotional copy and added primary provenance and deprecation notes. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after original and later technical-source checks. This is a distinct named API release configuration, not an assertion of a separately trained weight set.
